'''''Phoenix roebelenii''''', with common names of '''dwarf date palm''',<ref>[https://www.gardenia.net/plant/phoenix-roebelenii Palmpedia]</ref> '''pygmy date palm''', '''miniature date palm''' or '''robellini palm''', is a [[species]] of [[Phoenix (plant)|date palm]] [[native plant|native]] to southeastern Asia, from southwestern China ([[Yunnan]] [[Provinces of China|Province]]), northern [[Laos]] and northern [[Vietnam]] (in Dien Bien Province, Ha Giang Province, Cao Bang Province, Lang Son Province).<ref name="POWO">{{cite web | title=Phoenix roebelenii O'Brien | website=Plants of the World Online | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:668945-1 | access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 10 January 2018}}</ref>

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''roebelenii'' honours the orchid collector [[Carl Roebelen]] (1855–1927).<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

==Description==
''Phoenix roebelenii'' is a small to medium-sized, slow-growing slender [[tree]] growing to {{convert|2|-|7|m|ft|abbr=}} tall.  The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{convert|60|-|120|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, [[pinnate]], with around 100 leaflets arranged in a single plane (unlike the related ''[[Phoenix loureiroi|P. loureiroi]]'' where the leaflets are in two planes). Each leaflet is {{convert|15|-|25|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and 1 cm wide, slightly drooping, and grey-green in colour with scurfy pubescence below.

The [[flower]]s are small, yellowish, produced on a {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} [[inflorescence]]. The [[fruit]] is an edible 1 cm [[drupe]] resembling a small, thin-fleshed [[Date (fruit)|date]].<ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref>

==Cultivation and uses==
''Phoenix roebelenii'' is a popular [[ornamental plant]] in gardens in tropical and subtropical  climate areas. With a minimum temperature requirement of {{convert|-3|C|}}, it is grown under glass or as a [[houseplant]] in cooler areas.<ref>{{cite web | last=Palms | first=NZ | title=P. roebelenii | website=NZ Palms | url=https://nzpalms.co.nz/species/Phoenix-roebelenii.html | access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref><ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> It needs little pruning to develop a strong structure, is resistant to pests, is tolerant to soil variation, and is moderately drought tolerant. The plant grows in partial shade to full sun, with the local climate determining where to plant.

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phoenix roebelenii'' | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/12771/Phoenix-roebelenii/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 77 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 25 April 2018}}</ref>

The [[NASA Clean Air Study]] concluded that this was a plant that was effective at removing common household air toxins [[formaldehyde]] and [[benzene]].
